spec.prompt: Deep snow in the Ural taiga, grey late-afternoon light. The hatch cover of the scorched spherical Voskhod-2 capsule (first reference) drops away from a pale birch trunk and falls into the snow. the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov (face and suit exactly as in his reference images), in his white Berkut suit with rust-orange straps, no helmet, bare head, climbs out through the round hatch and sinks waist-deep into the snow, breath steaming; he turns and reaches back to help the commander Pavel Belyayev (also a white spacesuit, bare head, no helmet) climb out behind him. Only these two men. Medium-wide shot at snow level, the capsule on one side, open snow and forest on the other. Photorealistic, shot on 35mm film, documentary realism. March 1965, the Ural taiga of Perm Oblast: dense snow-covered spruce and pale birch forest, waist-deep snow, breath steaming at -25 C. A red-orange-and-white parachute hangs snagged in the treetops. Accurate 1965 Soviet details only: no modern clothing or gear, no orange coveralls, no helmets. Clear readable subjects, uncluttered frame. No on-screen text, no captions.
